title: Scheduled multi-protocol customer exports with SFTP fallback and upload integrity attestations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a robust scheduled export flow that supports multiple delivery protocols (S3, GCS, webhook) with an automatic SFTP fallback for tenants that require on-prem transfer. Exports must include an integrity attestation bundle (SHA256 checksums plus KMS-signed manifest) to allow customers to validate uploads without exposing raw keys. The feature should respect per-tenant delivery preferences, failure budgets, and provide clear observability for export success/failure and fallback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduled exports can be configured per-tenant to prefer: S3, GCS, webhook, or SFTP fallback.
When primary delivery fails after configurable retry budget, system switches a single-export to SFTP fallback and records an auditable reason.
Export payloads are accompanied by a manifest.json containing file checksums and a KMS-backed signature; customers can verify integrity using public key material.
All export attempts (primary + fallback) are visible in Console: status, bytes, latency, retries, and failure reason.
Retry budget and SFTP-queue throttling prevent noisy tenant from impacting global export throughput.
End-to-end integration tests that simulate webhook downtime, S3 permission errors, and high concurrency pass in CI.
Signed manifest schema and KMS key rotation plan documented and approved by security.
At least one pilot customer (mid-market) completes successful scheduled export to SFTP using the new flow and validates checksums.
updates: 2026-02-18: Spike completed to evaluate SFTP gateway options. We prototyped a lightweight SFTP transfer worker using existing export staging buckets and a short-lived signed URL pull model to avoid storing credentials on workers.
2026-02-24: Decision: use SHA256 checksums + KMS asymmetric signing (RSA-2048) for manifests to simplify customer verification. HMAC rejected because of key-sharing complexity across tenants.
2026-02-28: Design review with Security. Security requested explicit key-rotation docs and the ability to audit signature verification attempts. Added security_review_required flag.
2026-03-03: Implemented protocol-preference config field on tenant export profile (console + API). Backend reads preference and enqueues export job with preferred delivery sequence.

2026-03-05: Integration test showing webhook endpoint returning 503 leads to automatic retry then SFTP fallback after 3 failed attempts. Observability metrics show fallback_count incremented; created dashboards panel 'exports.fallback.rate'.

2026-03-08: Load test (concurrent 200 scheduled exports) shows SFTP fallback worker saturating CPU during intensive SSH handshake surge. Throttling added to SFTP-queue and connection re-use implemented in worker to reduce CPU by ~45%.
2026-03-10: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4567 implementing manifest signer + Console UI for export audit. QA preparing pilot.
Next steps: finalize KMS key rotation playbook, implement tenant-level retry budget UI, finish security sign-off, run pilot with customer 'AcmeAI' (requested SFTP).
notes: Trade-offs considered: HMAC-based attestation would be cheaper CPU-wise but requires secure key distribution to customers; RSA signing chosen to avoid key-sharing and to provide a stable public verification path.
Failure mode: if KMS signing fails, system writes an unsigned manifest and marks export status as 'signed_manifest_failed' with clear instructions for customer support to escalate.
Operational runbook: on repeated SFTP queue saturation, increase worker pool in 'dedicated-exporters' autoscaling group and raise SFTP connection re-use limit.
Observability: added metrics exports.fallback.count, exports.manifest.sign_latency_ms, exports.sftp.queue_depth. Alert rule: fallback rate > 0.5% sustained for 30m triggers pager.
Privacy: manifest contains only filenames, sizes, and checksums. No PII or token data is included.
